newsitem.title: USA: Thai problems won't end E.Asia miracle--World Bank.
newsitem.headline: Thai problems won't end E.Asia miracle--World Bank.

text.p: Problems in Thailand, where the authorities are seeking assistance from the International Monetary Fund, will not signal the end of the "East Asia miracle", a senior World Bank official said on Thursday.
Javad Khalilzadeh-Shirazi, acting vice president for the bank's East Asia and Pacific region, said in a statement that the economies in the region remained in good shape.

"Many have high savings rates, low or non-existent fiscal deficits and a strong export base," he said. "However there is a growing realization that large current account deficits, especially those financed by short-term borrowing, are not sustainable in the long term."

The statement said that the World Bank backed Thailand's decision to formulate a program of IMF-backed reforms and that the World Bank was prepared "to support the government in its structural reform efforts."
Another bank official said this did not appear to be a sign that the bank would offer financial support in addition to anything on offer from the IMF.

"If Thailand is able to put in place a sound economic reform program, especially in partnership with the IMF and other multilateral and bilateral financing sources, it should be able to stabilize its financial situation rather quickly and help ensure continued access to external capital," Shirazi said.

"Of course implementing such a program will require sacrifices and difficult reforms, but the government can build on its reputation for generally good economic management in years prior to the crisis, its still strong position in export markets and its history of good fiscal performance."
Thai officials said on Monday that they were looking for help from the IMF and that this could take the form of a loan.
It would be the first IMF loan to Thailand for more than 10 years and would probably be tied to conditions on government spending, inflation and reform of the banking sector.
